title: Domu: A Child's Dream
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Police investigate a string of deaths in a Tokyo apartment complex that look like rooftop jumps and throat-slashings. The killer is 'Old Cho', a seemingly senile resident with psychic powers, and only Etsuko, a newly arrived eight-year-old with powers of her own, knows it; their hidden battle engulfs the building (Dark Horse blurb via AniList and MU; Manga Bookshelf review).
life_message: A child's fierce sense of right can stand up to cruelty that adults cannot even see.

content.note: Murders staged as falls and throat-slashings (Manga Bookshelf); Gore tag (AniList); MU Murder/s, Cruelty, Violence. Reviewer says older teens.
'Intensely creepy' psychological thriller with palpable dread (Manga Bookshelf); Horror, Psychological (MU).
Deaths disguised as suicides (Manga Bookshelf); AniList Suicide tag (low rank); MU Mind Break.
Psychic powers are fantastic, not imitable.

dominant: Moral courage of a child against cruelty; abuse of power critiqued; urban alienation

frames.aligns: Etsuko's moral courage defends neighbors from a murderer.
Evil of a hidden destroyer is exposed.
frames.concerns: Gore and dread disturb the heart.

frames.aligns: A child stands for right against evil.
Truthful picture of sin, not made attractive.
Courage on behalf of the vulnerable.
Clear framing of good and evil.

frames.concerns: Climax is a violent psychic battle.

frames.aligns: Attention to the vulnerable in a neglected housing block.
Cho's greed for 'treasures' shown as cruel craving.
Power used to harm is rejected.
Mental power, ethics in using it.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Police investigation runs alongside; no honor code (Manga Bookshelf).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Police try to restore order; Etsuko acts outside it (Manga Bookshelf).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Neighbors in a housing block, not family, are at stake (MU Apartment Life).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: A child outmatches the adults (Manga Bookshelf).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Psychic powers in a modern secular city (MU).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival against a killer drives the story (Dark Horse blurb).

folkways.japan: Set in a 1980s Japanese danchi (public housing estate), reflecting period anxieties about isolation in new urban blocks.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer describes a 'taut psychological thriller' of mood and dread, not lessons (Manga Bookshelf).
delivery.note: Moral contrast between Cho and Etsuko is left to the reader inside a thriller.

winners_losers: Etsuko, 'fiercely moral and incredibly brave', gets the sympathy; Cho, 'a childish adult', is the threat (Manga Bookshelf).
to_verify: Exact graphic level of the deaths and the final psychic battle.
Whether any child is harmed or killed.
Suicide tag on AniList is low-ranked; deaths are disguised murders per the review.
